decision: Make duration-bound observed-time calibration the only qualification-grade Qubes resource evidence path; first close QA coverage drift, then disable the legacy fixed-interval executable entrypoint.

reviews.preferred: duration-bound CLI with observed sample offsets
reviews.reason: The canonical DAG is 210ms; a fixed 1000ms interval can measure idle/post-workload state and understate resource demand. The duration-bound path derives 52ms for five samples and validates observed offsets.

reviews.preferred: fail closed on unsafe explicit intervals and preserve the low-level sampler only as a library/test primitive
reviews.reason: Silent clamping or keeping two qualification-grade executables permits evidence with incompatible temporal guarantees.

reviews.preferred: thin duration-bound authority over the existing sampler
reviews.reason: It adds no qrexec calls, no workload extension, no daemon/database, and keeps runtime mutation semantics unchanged.

alternatives.name: legacy fixed 1000ms CLI
alternatives.failure: sampling window can exceed a short DAG workload and contaminate calibration with idle measurements

alternatives.name: stretch or repeat workload to fit a fixed interval
alternatives.failure: changes workload semantics and increases CPU/resource cost

alternatives.name: duration-bound CLI authority
alternatives.benefits: correct temporal evidence, fail-closed explicit interval validation, observed timing, minimal overhead

qa.legacy_1000ms: must fail closed for the canonical workload

lesson: A safety/correctness primitive is not a release gate until the executable path and the independent QA shard both exercise it.
next: Disable or delegate the legacy direct qubes-resource-calibration-harness executable so no operational path can emit qualification-grade resource evidence without duration-bound observed timing; add hosted/local parity coverage for that migration.
